question.text: The flat base of a hemisphere of radius a with no charge inside it lies in a horizontal plane. A uniform electric field $\vec{E}$ is applied at an angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$ with the vertical direction. The electric flux through the curved surface of the hemisphere is

solution.text:
We know that,
$$
\phi=\oint E \cdot d S=E \oint d S \cos 45^{\circ}
$$
In case of hemisphere
$$
\phi_{\text {curved }}=\phi_{\text {circular }}
$$
Therefore, $\phi_{\text {curved }}=E \pi a^2 \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{E \pi a^2}{\sqrt{2}}$
